title: indigo_agent_scheduler: compute only the first run of the plan without night hooks, every plan was computed twice when night hooks are named
description:
Performance follow-up from the scheduler performance study (scratchpad perf/, i5-9400, -O3; Raspberry Pi 4 about 5-10x slower).

When night hooks are named, update_plan() computes two full night plans at every recomputation (each decision and every IDLE_CHECK_INTERVAL while a task runs): plan #1 without night hooks and plan #2 with them. Plan #1 is used only for plan_first_run and, before the night starts, for `work`; both need only the first non-running run. With DEFER_GAIN > 0 a decision followed by start_task() computes 4 full plans (select_deferred -> update_plan, then process() after plan_dirty), about 240 ms on the heavy queue (1.2-2.4 s on a Pi).

Proposal (exact): when hooks will be added, call plan #1 with max_runs = number of running entries + 1; if that first run starts before `from` (rare), fall back to the full plan. Measured: the first-run-only plan 0.007-0.11 ms vs 17-62 ms for the full plan, same first run. Halves every plan computation when night hooks are configured. Also consider not recomputing after start_task() when the decision's plan already covers it, if it can be kept exact (careful input key: release_holds leaves deferred_from labels, `now` enters init_state).

Tests: integration tests with night hooks named showing identical plans and decisions; a unit or timing check. Results must not change.
